## Plan

### Mechanics summary
- Three phases. First phase HP 100 `[GAME-EXTRACT]`. Each new phase adds HP; community totals differ (about 600) `[COMMUNITY]`.
- Moves `[GAME-EXTRACT]`:
  - Bite: 20
  - Skull Bash: 14 + Vulnerable
  - Pounce: 30
  - Multi-Claw: 10×?
  - Lacerate: 10×3
  - Big Pounce: 45
  - Burning Growl: adds Burns, +2 Strength
- Revives with new powers each phase `[GAME-EXTRACT]`:
  - Painful Stabs: unblocked damage adds Wounds
  - Nemesis: gains Intangible at turn end
  - Adaptable: revive
- Phase 1 punishes Skills, granting Strength per Skill played `[COMMUNITY]`. The game data gives it **Enrage** from the start (`AfterCardPlayed: Gain Amount Strength`) `[GAME-EXTRACT]`; the summary does not show a card-type filter, so it may count every card played. Until the first fight shows which, assume each card played adds Strength and play fewer, bigger cards in phase 1 `[HYPOTHESIS]`.
- **Second sources (2026-11-19 search summaries of several guides):** phases of 100, 200 and 300 HP (600 in all), a one-turn stun between phases, and phase 1's Enrage gives **2 Strength for each Skill** you play `[COMMUNITY]`. Phase 2's Painful Stabs adds a Wound for each unblocked hit.
- **The wiki, phase by phase** `[COMMUNITY]` (slaythespire.wiki.gg page, accessed 2026-11-19): **phase 1** 100 HP (111 at A8+), Enrage 2 per Skill (3 at A9), Bite 20 and Skull Bash 14 + 1 Vulnerable alternating; **phase 2** 200 HP (212), Painful Stabs (Wounds into your discard pile on each unblocked attack hit), Multi-Claw 10×3 every turn gaining one hit each use, Enrage gone; **phase 3** 300 HP (313), Nemesis (Intangible 1 at the end of every other turn), Lacerate 10×3, Big Pounce 45, Burning Growl (3 Burns, +2 Strength), repeating. Each phase revives it (Adaptable). Plan: few Skills in phase 1; block fully in phase 2 (every unblocked hit adds Wounds, and Multi-Claw grows); in phase 3 save damage for the turns without Intangible and block Big Pounce 45.
- `tools/plan_turn.py` reads Enrage from the state and adds its amount to each hit of the intent for every Skill a plan plays: in phase 1, attack and keep Skills for when they are needed.
- Nemesis (phase 2 onward) gives it 1 Intangible at the end of its turns `[GAME-EXTRACT]`, which makes alternate turns the damage windows; Painful Stabs adds a Wound when its attacks deal damage `[GAME-EXTRACT]`.

### Deck checklist
- **Countable checks** (`tools/deck_check.py`, tuned on the history 2026-11-19) `[PLAYER-DATA, weak]`: multi-hit attacks at least 1 (burst on tangible turns; survived 1.3, fatal 0.6).
- **Sustained damage** over the longest fight in the game (median 10 turns).
- **Block for 30 and 45 hits.** Impervious is ideal for Big Pounce.
- **Phase 1: attack-heavy.** Avoid playing many Skills while it gains Strength from them.
- **Phase 2: block fully.** Unblocked damage adds Wounds, so exhaust outlets help.
- **Phase 3: burst on turns it is tangible.**

### HP target on arrival
- Ironclad benchmark: median 44, p90 63. **Rest if HP is below about 54.** Survived fights arrived at a median 92% HP (all characters).

### First three turns
- Phase 1: attacks only where possible. Each phase ends with a stun turn, which is free setup.

### Potion plan
- Block potions for Pounce and Big Pounce. Damage potions on tangible turns in phase 3.

### What killed the Player here, and the counter
- Ironclad: 0 of 5 fatal (all characters: 8 of 29). `[PLAYER-DATA]`
- Main risk is running out of HP over three phases. Carry an Act 3 scaling engine.

### The Agent's fights here (2026-11-22)
- **Record** `[OBS]` (run benchmark 16, A0, simulator on v0.111.1): 3 of 24 fights won, where the Player won all 5 as Ironclad. Many were lost from full or nearly full HP (`reports/phase9/run-bench-16.md` section 5).
- **Why, in part: the fight search's value of a lost rollout pointed the wrong way across the forms** `[OBS]` (`reports/phase9/boss-replay-2.md` section 6). It counted the HP of the form alive only, so losing in the first form looked closer to a win than losing in the second, and the search kept away from killing the first form: in a traced fight it played 7 cards in 5 turns and died with the first form at 33 HP. With the forms to come counted (100, 200 and 300 HP; 111, 212 and 313 at A8+ `[GAME]`), the same fight reaches the third form. Whether the correction wins fights is what boss replay 2 measures.
- **The correction, measured** `[OBS]` (boss replay 2, 2026-11-22, `reports/phase9/boss-replay-2.md` section 6): with the forms to come counted, the search removes 70% of the three forms' HP against 31% over 27 situations and ends in the third form or wins in 29 of 35 fights, where it used to die in the first or second in 32 of 35. Fights won: 2 of 23 with the Agent's decks either way; with the Player's decks 4 of 12 against 0 of 12. On by default since 2026-11-22 18:50 (`tools/sim.py LOSS_COUNTS_FORMS`). The fight is still mostly lost: with the Agent's decks it ends in the third form with about 190 of 300 HP left.
- **A traced third form** `[OBS]` (one fight, the same section, note of 18:10): lost with the boss at 26 HP. Every rollout was lost at 36 of 40 decisions, and six sampled worlds did not tell one card's worth apart, so on turn 1 the turn ended with three playable cards in hand; on the first Intangible turn the hand held no block card and three attacks went in for 3 damage. `[HYPOTHESIS]` More sampled worlds where candidates are close, or no end of turn inside the noise, would win some of the close ones; the deck's block (three Defends and one Flame Barrier in 29 cards) is the larger part.
- **What guides advise** `[COMMUNITY]` (one guide read in full on 2026-11-22, early access, no patch named): the first form is a sprint (kill its 100 HP with attacks before its Strength builds; do not spend the first turns on block and draw); in the second form block every hit in full (each unblocked hit adds a Wound); in the third defend on the Intangible turns and spend damage on the others. A deck made of damage alone wins the first form and fails in the third; for the Ironclad a scaling power (Demon Form) and block that carries over (Barricade, Calipers) are named. Damage over time is cleared at each new form. This agrees with the checklist above and with the direction of the correction: the first form is to be killed fast, which is what the search avoided.
